title: Discovery - Model selection & deployment options - Mariner Systems
summary: Initial discovery focused on selecting open models and deployment mode. Customer needs 32k+ context for document QA, multilingual support (EN/FR/ES), and function/tool-calling for retrieval + actions. Security and data residency may push toward Dedicated/Private. Agreed to run a benchmark pilot and share security pack.
next_steps: Maya to send tailored pricing and Dedicated sizing options (by 2026-05-08)
Diego to run initial latency/cost estimates and propose model candidates (by 2026-05-11)
Priya to share sample prompts, dataset slice and expected SLAs (by 2026-05-10)
Schedule technical deep-dive + proof-of-concept kickoff (proposed week of 2026-05-18)
action_items: Diego Alvarez - run model latency & throughput bench for 8k/32k contexts, include quantized variants (due 2026-05-11)
Maya Chen - send pricing, Dedicated/reserved capacity options, and security summary (SOC2, ISO, KMS notes) (due 2026-05-08)
Priya Nair - upload 200 sample docs and prompt templates to shared S3 link (due 2026-05-10)
Tom Sullivan - confirm if VPC peering / private deployment is a hard requirement or preference (due 2026-05-09)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-06 15:00 PDT | Duration: 00:52:00 | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Mariner Head of ML), Tom Sullivan (Mariner CTO), Alicia Park (Mariner PM)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. We're kicking off, we've got about 50 minutes on the calendar. Quick intros - Diego from my team is our solutions engineer who will do most of the technical deep dive.
[00:12] Priya (Mariner): Hi all, Priya here. We're evaluating models and deployment options for our document QA pipeline, lots of lengthy docs, multi-language UX.
[00:20] Tom (Mariner): Tom - CTO - interested in tradeoffs, cost, and whether we go hosted or private for compliance.
[00:24] Alicia (Mariner): Alicia - PM, mostly product requirements and timelines.
[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): Great. Can I start by asking a couple of baseline q's about context length and languages?
[00:34] Priya: Sure - primary need is 32k context for legal and research docs, sometimes we need 65k for stitched reports but that's less common. Also need EN, FR, ES support, some JA/KO on lower priority.
[00:48] Diego: Okay that's helpful. For 32k we're typically looking at models that natively support long context or models with efficient windowing. Are you planning to do retriever + RAG with chunking, or want full single-pass context?
[00:58] Priya: Prefer single-pass for latency reasons, but we can do hybrid if cost is too high. Main SLO is sub-1.2s response for short queries, but for full-document summarization we can accept 3-5s.
[01:10] Maya: Good, and what's your throughput? Concurrent users or qps?
[01:14] Priya: Currently peak ~12 qps for embedding+generation combined during business hours, average is 3-4.
[01:20] Tom: We also need audit logs and encryption in transit+at rest, and we have EU data residency requirements for some customers.
[01:26] Diego: Noted on residency. That steers to Dedicated with region pinning, or Private if you need full on-prem/VPC. For SOC2/ISO we can share our compliance pack.
[01:36] Alicia: Also important - tool-calling: the model needs to call our internal knowledge base APIs and trigger actions like ticket creation. Is function-calling supported?
[01:45] Diego: Yes, function/tool calling is supported across our hosted and dedicated offerings; in Private you can run the same runtime with local integrations. A quick note - sometimes transcription or docs call it 'tool calling' or 'function calls', we support structured output and wrappers.
[01:58] Priya: What about open models? We're trying to avoid closed APIs for vendor lock-in. Which open weights do you recommend for 32k?
[02:06] Diego: For long context open models: variants like Mistral Long, Llama-2-70b with extended context patches, and some LlamaX variants are common. There's also the smaller-parameter long-context models (e.g., longformer-style or gptj with sparse attn) but they trade off quality. For multilingual, Llama-2 family is decent but Spanish/French are OK not perfect; Mistral has decent EU language coverage. There's also Falcon and RWKV variants; each has different perf/cost.
[02:34] Maya: We usually provide a model matrix - quality vs latency vs cost - and Diego can run quick bench on a short list. Any preferences on quantization?
[02:44] Priya: We're open to 4-bit quantized if quality holds up. Cost is a factor.
[02:49] Diego: Good. We'll include quantized and FP16 runs in benches. For function-calling, some open models need adapter layers or small finetunes to reliably produce structured JSON. There can be mis-parses, so we recommend a lightweight filter/validator in front.
[03:03] Tom: Latency targets - you'd mentioned sub-1.2s for short queries - can Redwood meet that on hosted? Or do we need Dedicated?
[03:12] Diego: On hosted, for smaller context lengths (<8k) it's usually achievable. For 32k single-pass with heavy decode, you'll typically see higher latency on shared hosted unless we pin Dedicated capacity. Dedicated with reserved GPUs will give predictable latencies and better throughput. Private can be as fast as Dedicated depending on hardware.
[03:29] Priya: Any recommendations for GPU type? We're looking at cost-effective but performant.
[03:34] Diego: For single-pass 32k the sweet spot is A100/RTX8000 class or Hopper if available; but quantized M40-style on T4s can be OK for lower concurrency. We'll scope recommended instance types in the sizing doc.
[03:47] Alicia: About costs - do you provide per-token breakdowns and ways to reduce unit cost?
[03:52] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost, KV/prefix cache savings, batching suggestions. Optimize features can recommend quantization and model swaps per workload.
[04:02] Priya: We're worried about hallucination on tool-calling and retrieval. Any best practices?
[04:07] Diego: Use strong retrieval + reranker, and for tool-calling always validate model output with a deterministic shim. We'll also recommend prompt engineering with instruction anchors and verification turns. We can instrument quality metrics in the console to alert on regressions.
[04:22] [04:22] Priya: (mumbles) And language quality - French legal terms must be precise.
[04:26] Diego: For high-precision legal language, sometimes we recommend an instruction-tuned model or a small domain-tune. We can help scope a small supervised fine-tune for critical flows.
[04:36] Tom: On security: we need KMS/HSM integration and SSO for users. Also audit logs for every inference.
[04:44] Maya: We support KMS integrations and comprehensive audit logs in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has audit logs too, but for strict residency or HSM requirements, Private is the route. I'll include the security pack.
[04:58] Alicia: Timeline - we'd like to run a POC in June and decide by end of Q3. Is that feasible?
[05:04] Maya: Yes, typical POC is 4-6 weeks. We'll propose success criteria in the POC plan.
[05:09] Diego: For the benchmark we suggest a short test: run 1k prompts across 8k and 32k contexts, measure latency, tokens/second, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy on a small eval set.
[05:20] Priya: That works. We'll share sample prompts and a dataset slice.
[05:24] [05:24] Diego: Quick question on tool-calling security - do your APIs accept signed JWTs or mTLS?
[05:30] Tom: We support JWTs and mTLS for internal services; for external conn we prefer mTLS.
[05:34] Diego: Great, that aligns with both Dedicated and Private integration patterns.
[05:38] [05:38] Maya: Anything else on compliance?
[05:40] Tom: Data retention settings - we need option to not persist customer data on hosted unless explicitly allowed.
[05:46] Maya: We have configurable retention policies and can scope no-retention for certain routes; Dedicated/Private gives you full control.
[05:53] Alicia: What about multilingual evals - can you run per-language quality tests?
[05:58] Diego: Yes, we'll include per-language BLEU/ROUGE-ish checks and human spot checks for FR/ES. For Japanese/Korean we might need a different model family or extra tuning.
[06:10] [06:10] Priya: Any limitations on streaming and partial output for long dumps? We need streaming so UI can show progressive answers.
[06:17] Diego: Streaming is supported. For very long decodes we often combine streaming with progressive retrieval + partial summarization to keep latency snappy.
[06:25] Maya: Alright, Diego will propose the model shortlist. Quick preference check - are you leaning Hosted to start and then Dedicated, or jump to Dedicated?
[06:33] Priya: Prefer to start Hosted for speed, but if latency/cost is bad we'll move to Dedicated. If residency or HSM is required, we may do Private directly.
[06:42] Maya: Makes sense. We'll show a path: hosted pilot -> dedicated sizing -> private if required.
[06:48] [06:48] Tom: For procurement, can you share contract terms and SLAs for Dedicated?
[06:52] Maya: Yes, I'll attach the Dedicated SLA and typical contract terms in the follow-up.
[06:57] Alicia: Any red flags or blockers from Redwood side?
[07:00] Diego: Nothing immediate. The main unknowns are model accuracy on your domain and exact concurrency profile; that's why the benchmark POC is important.
[07:09] Priya: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[07:12] Maya: Recap - Maya sends pricing, SLA, security pack. Diego runs benches and proposes model shortlist including quantized variants and per-language notes. Priya shares sample data and prompts. Schedule technical deep-dive and POC kickoff week of 2026-05-18.
[07:30] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:33] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links.
